decisions.name: NoteAndBugNoteAreDistinctConstructors
decisions.what: Note carries a plain string; BugNote marks a known wart
why: Chase.Render prints a BugNote with a 'BUG: ' prefix, so known warts stand out in the rendered %const line.
Severity could have been a separate field, but a two-constructor sum is simpler for the JSON parser, the renderer and the reader.
A third category (TODO, DEPRECATED) would be added here.

decisions.name: InvariantHasFourPartShape
decisions.what: Invariant = function name + ! lines + > consumes + optional hint
why: invLines and invConsumes render with different sigils (! and >) and mean different things: facts about the function, and pointers to its callers.
Separate list fields keep the JSON loader simple and the renderer mechanical.
invBodyHint is for the case where the body matters and the annotator wants to point the reader at it.

decisions.name: TestCoverageIsMaybeNotEmpty
decisions.what: chaseTestCoverage is Maybe [(Text, [TestRef])], not [(Text, [TestRef])]
why: Nothing means coverage analysis did not run; Just [] would mean it ran and found nothing. The two need to be told apart.
Chase.Render emits no ? lines for Nothing, and a ? line on every signature for Just, including 'no test references' for the uncovered ones.
Without the Maybe, a structure-only run and a covered run with no tests would render the same.

emptyChaseFile: sets chaseLanguage and chaseSourcePath from its arguments; chaseModuleName starts as '' and every list field starts empty
the structural fields are filled by extractStructure in Chase.Parse.Haskell and Chase.Parse.PureScript
chaseTestCoverage starts as Nothing; Chase.Coverage.attachCoverage sets it to Just when coverage runs
chaseParseErrors starts empty and nothing in chase ever adds to it
emptyAnnotations: sets annModName; annConstants, annInvariants, annDecisions, annOpenIssues and annTopologies start empty
chase-unison uses it when the annotations file has no entry for the project name

notes: sets invConsumes to [] and invBodyHint to Nothing
used by Chase.Annotations.Json.parseInvariantValue when an invariant is a plain array of strings

invHinted: sets invConsumes to [] and invBodyHint to Just the hint
nothing in chase calls it; parseObjectInvariant builds Invariant with the data constructor because it may need both consumes and a hint
constNote: an alias for the Note constructor; Chase.Annotations.Json.noteFromText builds notes with the constructors directly
constBug: an alias for the BugNote constructor; nothing in chase calls it
decision: an alias for the Decision constructor, arguments in field order: decName, decWhat, decWhy, decAffects
openIssue: an alias for the OpenIssue constructor, arguments in field order: oiName, oiWhat, oiWhy, oiBlocking, oiAffects

decisions.name: MissingIsEmptyMalformedIsAnError
decisions.what: loadAnnotations treats a missing file as an error; loadAnnotationsIfExists treats a missing file as no annotations; both return the parse error for a file that does not parse
why: chase's CLI resolves the path first and calls loadAnnotations, so an explicit -a path with a typo fails loudly.
chase-unison calls loadAnnotationsIfExists, because a project that has not been annotated yet is a normal state.

Until 2026-10-24 loadAnnotationsIfExists also returned no annotations for a file that failed to parse, so a typo in the file produced a bundle without annotations and no message. A malformed file is now always an error.

decisions.name: InvariantValueIsSumOfArrayOrObject
decisions.what: A JSON invariant value is either a plain array of strings or an object with structured fields
why: The array form keeps simple annotations short: ['line 1', 'line 2'] is enough when there is no intent, spec, consumes or hint.
The object form carries intent, effects, notes, spec, consumes and hint.
Any other JSON type is a parse error naming the function.

decisions.name: VersionFieldIsForwardCompatibility
decisions.what: The top-level 'version' field is checked; only version 1 is accepted
why: A version on every file turns a future format change into a one-line check.
A file without the field is read as version 1, so older files need no edit.

decisions.name: WriterMergesOneModule
decisions.what: writeModuleAnnotations replaces the given fields of one module and keeps everything else in the file
why: chase-annotate annotates one module per run. It used to write a file holding only that module, so annotating a second module deleted the first.
Constants and topologies are not generated, so a module's hand-written constants and topologies have to survive a regeneration.
The file is written to a .partial name and renamed into place, so a failure part way leaves the old file whole.

loadAnnotations.intent: Read and parse an annotations file, with the path in any error
notes: a missing file is Left 'annotations file not found: PATH'
an Aeson decode error and a parseRoot error are both Left with the path prefixed
consumes: app/Main.hs loadAnnotationsOrDie, which prints the Left and calls exitFailure

loadAnnotationsIfExists.intent: Annotations from a file that may not exist yet
notes: a missing file is Right Map.empty
an existing file goes through loadAnnotations, so a parse error is Left (probe U2)
consumes: app-unison/ChaseUnison.hs runExtract, which prints the Left and calls exitFailure

writeModuleAnnotations.intent: Merge one module's fields into an annotations file
notes: KM.union fields old: a given field replaces the module's field of the same name; fields not given are kept
a missing file is created holding only this module; createDirectoryIfMissing makes .inference if needed
a file that is not JSON, not an object, or not version 1 with a modules object is left untouched and the result is Left ending 'not overwritten'
writes PATH.partial with Pretty.encodePretty', two-space indent and keys sorted by compare, then renameFile onto PATH
hand-kept key order and blank lines are not preserved across a write, because the whole file is re-encoded

parseRoot: version defaults to 1 when absent; any other value fails with 'unsupported annotations version: N'
the modules object is required; when it is absent or not an object Aeson reports the error
parseModulesMap: keys are kept exactly as written via Key.toText, with no case folding

Chase.Pipeline.attachAnnotations looks a file up by its chaseModuleName, so a key that differs by one character attaches to nothing; Chase.Pipeline.unmatchedAnnotations reports such a key at the end of the run
parseModule: constants, invariants, decisions, openIssues and topologies are all optional and default to empty
the module key is copied into annModName
parseConstant: name and value are required; notes is optional and each note goes through noteFromText
noteFromText: only the exact prefix 'BUG: ', with the space, makes a BugNote; 'BUG:foo' stays a plain Note
the prefix is stripped from the BugNote's text; Chase.Render adds it back when rendering
parseInvariantsMap: one Invariant per key of the invariants object, in KM.toList order
the order has no effect on output: Chase.Render looks invariants up by name and prints them under the signatures in source order
parseInvariantValue: Array: parsed as [Text] and wrapped with Chase.Types.inv
any other JSON type fails with 'invariants.NAME must be an array of strings or an object'

notes: invLines are assembled in this order: 'intent: ...', 'effects: a, b', the notes as written, then one 'spec: input => expected' line per spec entry
consumes goes to invConsumes and hint goes to invBodyHint; neither is part of invLines
every field is optional; an empty object gives an Invariant with no lines, which Chase.Pipeline.checkAnnotationDrift does not flag

renderSpec: renders one SpecEntry as 'spec: INPUT => EXPECTED' with no escaping
parseDecision: name and what are required; why defaults to '' and affects to []
why goes through parseWhy, so it may be a string or an array of strings
parseOpenIssue: the same fields as parseDecision plus blocking, which defaults to []
parseWhy: a string is returned as it is; an array is joined with a single space by T.intercalate, so authors put their own punctuation at the end of each entry
any other JSON type fails with '<ctx> must be a string or array of strings'
parseTopology: name, vertices and transitions are required; transitions is an object from a vertex to the list of vertices it can move to, read pair by pair with Key.toText and AT.parseJSON
nothing checks that the vertices named in transitions appear in vertices

decisions.name: ProjectFoundFromTheSource
decisions.what: A project's .inference directory is found by walking up from the source being compressed, never from the working directory
why: chase used to look in the working directory first. open-slop recorded on 2026-10-17 that chase, run from chase's own checkout over open-slop's sources, attached chase's annotations to open-slop's modules.
Walking up from the source finds the project the source belongs to, wherever chase is started.
The walk stops at the first directory holding .git, so a checkout without .inference never picks up a parent directory's.

decisions.name: OneDirectoryForTheLlmTooling
decisions.what: chase's annotations, open-slop's .llmqignore and .llmqchase, and reference bundles all live in .inference at the project root
why: open-slop reads the same directory, so a repository set up for one tool is set up for the other.
Keeping the files out of the root keeps them out of the source tree; Chase.Sources.findSourceFiles does not enter directories whose name starts with a dot.

notes: makeAbsolute first; a file path starts the walk at takeDirectory of it
returns the first directory, from the start upward, that has a .inference directory
stops with Nothing at the first directory where doesPathExist (dir </> ".git") is true, so a worktree's .git file counts as well as a .git directory
also stops with Nothing at the filesystem root
consumes: app-unison/ChaseUnison.hs defaultAnnPath, which starts from "." because a codebase has no directory

notes: tries annotationFileNames in order inside the project's .inference: chase-annotation.json, then chase-annotations.json
Nothing when there is no project or neither file exists
the project's existing annotations file from locateAnnotations, else ROOT/.inference/chase-annotations.json
Nothing when the path is in no project with a .inference directory; chase-annotate then stops and asks for -o

decisions.name: OneWalkerForEveryScan
decisions.what: Source roots, test roots and the caller scan all find files with findSourceFiles
why: Chase.Pipeline and Chase.Callers had their own walkers before 2026-10-24. Neither skipped build output or dot-directories, and both followed symbolic links.
A link to a parent directory made the walk recurse until it ran out of stack or file handles, and a link to another checkout put that checkout's modules in this one's bundle (probe U4).
Run on a project root, the old walk compressed dist-newstyle's generated Paths_ modules.

notes: a root that is a file gives [root] when isSourceFile accepts it and [] otherwise; a root that does not exist gives [] without a warning
the root is used as given even when it is a symbolic link; links found inside the walk are skipped via pathIsSymbolicLink
directories for which skippedDirectory is true are not entered
entries are sorted with Data.List.sort at every level, so the result's order depends only on the tree

isSourceFile: accepts only takeExtension '.hs' and '.purs'; .lhs and .hsc are not read
case-sensitive: 'Foo.HS' is not a source file
skippedDirectory: true for any name starting with '.' (.git, .direnv, .inference) and for dist-newstyle, dist, .stack-work, .spago, output and node_modules
matches the directory's own name only, so a source directory called 'output' anywhere in the tree is skipped too

decisions.name: ExtensionBasedDispatch
decisions.what: parseSourceFile picks the parser by file extension: .hs goes to Chase.Parse.Haskell, .purs to Chase.Parse.PureScript
why: The two languages are parsed by unrelated libraries (ghc-lib-parser and the vendored PureScript CST), so there is no shared core to factor out.
The extension is the cheapest reliable signal; no need to read the file first.
Chase.Sources.findSourceFiles only returns .hs and .purs files, so the unsupported-extension branch is reached only by a caller passing some other path directly.

notes: takeExtension, case-sensitive: '.hs' -> Chase.Parse.Haskell.parseSourceFile, '.purs' -> Chase.Parse.PureScript.parseSourceFile
any other extension is Left ParseFailure 'unsupported source extension: EXT'

decisions.name: OneImportShapeForBothLanguages
decisions.what: Ref, ImportInfo and ImportNames are the language-neutral form both parsers produce for reference resolution
why: Chase.Coverage resolves a reference to its defining module the same way for Haskell and PureScript; only the extraction differs.
Chase.Parse.Haskell.importInfosOf builds ImportInfo from ghc-lib-parser's ImportDecl, and Chase.Parse.PureScript builds it from the CST's ImportDecl.
The module has no functions; the types are the whole contract.

decisions.name: ParserIsGhcLibParser
decisions.what: ghc-lib-parser is the parser; there is no hand-kept fixity or extension list
why: ghc-lib-parser is GHC's own parser as a library, so it accepts what GHC accepts, including GADT declarations with inline kind signatures, type families and standalone kind signatures.

The earlier backend was haskell-src-exts with a hand-kept extension and fixity list. It failed on a third of pelotero-engine's files on the 'data X :: Effect where' form, and the lists needed constant upkeep.
The cost is a large dependency closure and a hand-built Settings value (probedSettings and its helpers) that has to match the ghc-lib-parser version's record fields.

decisions.name: RawAstExposedForCoverage
decisions.what: parseHsModule is exported alongside parseSourceFile and returns the HsModule and the source text
why: Chase.Coverage walks a test file's AST for references and imports, which the ChaseFile skeleton has thrown away.
Exporting parseHsModule keeps the parser set-up (probedSettings, applySourcePragmas, preprocessCpp) in one place.
parseSourceFile is parseHsModule followed by extractStructure.

decisions.name: PragmasReadFromSourceTextNotAst
decisions.what: LANGUAGE pragmas for the %ext line are read by a textual scan of the source preamble
why: Pragmas are not declarations, so they are not in hsmodDecls.
Reading them from the text is direct and does not depend on how a ghc-lib-parser version represents them.

decisions.name: HeadOnlyForClassAndInstance
decisions.what: ClassDecl and instance declarations render only their first line
why: Class bodies are method signatures, which extractSignatures already emits; printing the body as well would show them twice.
Instance bodies are method definitions, and chase leaves out function bodies everywhere.

decisions.name: ExtensionImplicationsAppliedExplicitly
decisions.what: applySourcePragmas sets TemplateHaskellQuotes whenever a file enables TemplateHaskell
why: xopt_set sets exactly the named extension. It does not follow impliedXFlags, the table of extensions that enable others; GHC's driver does that, and chase runs the parser without the driver.
The lexer rule for '$(' splices is gated on TemplateHaskellQuotes, so without this a file with -XTemplateHaskell fails with 'parse error on input $'.
This is the only implication that has broken parsing so far; another would be added in applyOne.

decisions.name: CppHandledByLineBlanking
decisions.what: In a file with LANGUAGE CPP, every line whose first non-space character is '#' is replaced by an empty line; both branches of #if/#else are kept
why: ghc-lib-parser does no preprocessing, and Grace.Compat failed with 'parse error on input #' before this.
Blanking rather than deleting keeps every line number, so the AST's SrcSpans still index the original lines.
Both branches are kept on purpose: Grace.Compat has two fromAesonMap signatures, one per branch, and the skeleton shows both.
cpphs was rejected because cabal's MIN_VERSION_pkg macros are undefined outside a cabal build, and because it keeps only one branch.
A conditional that splits one expression across branches, or code that depends on a #define, fails to parse and is reported like any other parse failure.

parseHsModule.intent: Parse one .hs file with ghc-lib-parser and return the source text and the HsModule, or a ParseFailure
notes: reads with BS.readFile and decodes with TE.decodeUtf8, which throws on invalid UTF-8 instead of returning a ParseFailure
runs preprocessCpp before building the StringBuffer; the text returned is the preprocessed text, so SrcSpans index T.lines of it
applySourcePragmas runs before initParserOpts, because the parser options fix the extension bits when they are built
a failed parse is Left with getPsErrorMessages rendered through ppr
parseHsModule, then extractStructure over the preprocessed text and its T.lines

preprocessCpp: returns the text unchanged unless needsCpp is true
tests each line with T.stripStart before looking for '#', so indented directives are blanked too
pragma lines start with '{-#', not '#', so they survive and applySourcePragmas still sees them
needsCpp: true when pragmasFromSource lists exactly 'CPP'; matching is case-sensitive, as GHC's is
applySourcePragmas: reads the pragmas with getOptions on the buffer and folds applyOne over them
only '-X' flags are applied, via parseExtensionFlag; OPTIONS_GHC and -W flags are dropped
an extension name that is not a LangExt.Extension constructor is ignored without a warning
parseExtensionFlag: accepts '-XName' and finds the LangExt.Extension whose show equals Name by scanning [minBound .. maxBound]
'-XNoName' forms are not recognised, so a pragma that turns an extension off is ignored
extractStructure: fills chaseModuleName, chaseExtensions, chaseFixities, chaseImports, chaseSignatures, chasePatterns and chaseDataDecls
constants, invariants, decisions, open issues and topologies stay empty until Chase.Pipeline.attachAnnotations
moduleNameOf: the module name from hsmodName; '' for a file without a module header

notes: impQualifiedOnly is true unless ideclQualified is NotQualified, so both 'import qualified M' and 'import M qualified' count
impAlias comes from ideclAs
an Exactly import list that contains an IEThingAll (T(..)) counts as ImportAll, because the constructors and fields it brings in are not listed by name
an EverythingBut list becomes ImportHiding with the names from ieNames

importsOf: each import pretty-printed through ppr and showSDocUnsafe; Chase.Render.collapseImport later drops the name list
extractSignatures: top-level TypeSig and ClassOpSig, and the signatures inside each ClassDecl's tcdSigs, all in one list
a class method has its plain name, so two classes with a method of the same name give two Signatures with that sigName
in a CPP file both branches of an #if can give a Signature with the same sigName
extractClassSig: one LSig from a class body, handed to sigToSignatures
sigToSignatures: TypeSig and ClassOpSig give one Signature per name, all sharing the declaration's verbatim text and start line
SPECIALISE, INLINE, fixity and other Sig forms give no Signature here; FixSig is read by extractFixity
extractPatternSig: PatSynSig declarations as (name, start line, verbatim) triples for mergePatterns
extractPatternBind: PatSynBind declarations; the name is read from the source text by patternNameFromSource, not from the AST
patternNameFromSource: after 'pattern', a '(' means an operator name up to ')'; otherwise the first token, unless the next token is an operator, in which case that operator is the name (infix pattern synonyms)
Nothing when the text does not start with 'pattern'
mergePatterns: joins a pattern's signature and binding by name into one Pattern whose verbatim text is the signature, a newline, then the binding
the line is the signature's when there is one, else the binding's; the result is sorted by patSrcLine
extractFixity: FixSig declarations; fixOps comes from fixityOpsFromSource on the verbatim text
fixityOpsFromSource: strips infixl, infixr or infix and the precedence digits, then T.splitOn ',' and T.strip on each part
an operator written in backticks keeps its backticks
extractDataDecl: DataDecl, SynDecl and FamDecl render their whole span; ClassDecl and ClsInstD render their first line
an instance's cddName is its head pretty-printed through ppr, such as 'A.FromJSON SpecEntry', because an instance has no name of its own
data family instances and type family instances (DataFamInstD, TyFamInstD) give nothing
rdrNameToText: occNameString of rdrNameOcc: the name without any qualifier
startLine: srcSpanStartLine of a RealSrcSpan; 0 for an UnhelpfulSpan
sliceSourceSpan: lines srcSpanStartLine to srcSpanEndLine of the span, joined with newlines
take and drop are total, so a span past the end of the file gives a shorter text, never a crash; an UnhelpfulSpan gives ''
sliceFirstLine: only the span's first line; '' for an UnhelpfulSpan or a line past the end
pragmasFromSource: scans only the preamble: blank lines and lines starting with '--', '{-' or '#'
splits each LANGUAGE pragma's body on ',' and strips each name; OPTIONS_GHC and other pragmas are skipped
lines starting with '#' count as preamble, so needsCpp can find LANGUAGE CPP below an early #if
probedSettings: a Settings.Settings with genericPlatform and empty tool paths; the parser reads only extensions and parser options from the DynFlags built on it
the ToolSettings and PlatformMisc field sets match a particular ghc-lib-parser release; a release that adds fields fails to compile here with 'Not in scope' or a missing-field warning

decisions.name: VendoredCstParserNotLineScanner
decisions.what: PureScript is parsed with a vendored copy of the purs compiler's CST library (Chase.Vendor.PureScript.CST.*) instead of the earlier column-0 line scanner
why: The line scanner anchored on column-0 lines and broke on unusual formatting, lost continuation lines in class method signatures and mishandled instance chains.
A real parser gives each declaration form a typed case, so a new CST constructor shows up as an incomplete-pattern warning rather than a silent miss.
The vendored copy keeps purescript-cst's release cadence and dependency closure out of chase; chase code imports only the Chase.Vendor modules.
The vendored copy has to be resynced by hand when PureScript adds syntax.

decisions.name: TwoStageParseViaResFull
decisions.what: PSParser.parseModule gives a partial result, and resFull on it gives the full Module; either stage can fail
why: This is the upstream compiler's own two-stage shape: the first stage parses the header and imports, the second the declarations.
Both stages report NonEmpty CSTErr.ParserError, and parseCstFile formats both with renderParserErrors, so callers see one message format.

decisions.name: DeclRangesByNextDeclStart
decisions.what: Each declaration ends on the line before the next declaration starts; the last ends at the file's last line
why: The CST has spans for tokens and sub-nodes but no single span for a declaration with its trailing lines.
Every line between two declaration starts belongs to the earlier one, and sliceLines drops trailing blank lines so the text stays tight.
A comment above a declaration is therefore printed at the end of the declaration before it.

decisions.name: ForeignImportsAreSeparateFromSignatures
decisions.what: foreign import declarations go to chaseForeignImports, not chaseSignatures, and all three forms (value, data, kind) share one extractor
why: A foreign import is backed by a JavaScript file, so changing one usually means changing that file too; Chase.Render prints them under their own %foreign header.
They share the Signature type with ordinary signatures, so the renderer and drift checker treat them alike.

decisions.name: HeadOnlyForClassInstanceDerive
decisions.what: DeclClass, DeclInstanceChain and DeclDerive render only their first line
why: Class bodies are method signatures, which extractClassMethods already emits.
Instance bodies are method definitions, and chase leaves out function bodies everywhere.
This matches decision HeadOnlyForClassAndInstance in Chase.Parse.Haskell.

decisions.name: ClassMethodsAndTopLevelSigsAreFlattened
decisions.what: Class method signatures follow the top-level signatures in the one chaseSignatures list
why: Invariants attach by name, whether the name is a top-level binding or a class method.
A top-level signature and a class method with the same name give two Signatures; an invariant for that name then renders under both, because Chase.Render looks it up once per Signature.

decisions.name: SelfReferencesFilteredTwice
decisions.what: valueBindingRefs drops an unqualified reference to the binding's own name, and Chase.Coverage.buildTestIndex drops self-references again for both languages
why: A recursive helper would otherwise be listed as tested by itself.
buildTestIndex's filter compares the resolved module and name, so it also catches a qualified self-reference; the filter here is older and is now redundant but harmless.

openIssues.name: InstanceChainTailIgnored
openIssues.what: For a DeclInstanceChain only the first instance head produces a data declaration; the 'else instance' clauses produce nothing
why: extractDataDecl matches 'CST.Separated h _' and drops the tail.
For 'instance fooString :: Foo String ... else instance fooDefault :: Foo a ...' only the first head is printed.
The fix is to emit one head-only ChaseDataDecl per element of the tail.
blocking: a complete picture of classes that use instance chains

openIssues.name: DeclRoleAndKindSignatureProduceNoOutput
openIssues.what: Standalone kind signatures and role declarations take part in declRanges but no extractor prints them
why: declStartLine handles DeclKindSignature and DeclRole so that neighbouring declarations get the right line ranges, but extractDataDecl and extractSignature return Nothing for them.

A module that declares 'data Foo :: Type -> Type' before 'data Foo a = ...' shows the data declaration without its kind signature, and its kind signature lines are printed at the end of the previous declaration.
The fix is an extractor for both forms and somewhere in ChaseFile to put the result, which touches Chase.Types and Chase.Render.
blocking: complete output for modules with standalone kind signatures or role declarations

openIssues.name: OperatorReferencesNotCollected
openIssues.what: Operator uses give no Ref: collectFromExpr returns [] for ExprOpName and walks only the operands of ExprOp
why: A PureScript operator is an alias, declared with a fixity declaration, for a named function. A test that uses '<>' or a project's own operator does not credit the function it aliases.
ExprInfix (backtick application) does walk its operator expression, so 'a `foo` b' credits foo.
blocking: coverage for functions that tests reach only through an operator

openIssues.name: ClassMethodSignaturesAreFirstLineOnly
openIssues.what: toMethodSig takes only the first source line of a class method signature, so a method whose type spans several lines loses the rest
why: The CST has the full type, but its pretty-printer normalises the formatting, so the text is sliced from the source instead.
The fix is to slice from the method's name token to the last line of its type's span.
blocking: faithful output for class methods with multi-line types

notes: parseCstFile, then extractStructure on the source text and Module

scanTestBindings.intent: A .purs file's module name, imports, and one (name, line, refs) entry per top-level value binding
notes: the imports come from importInfo over CST.modImports, for Chase.Coverage.resolveRef
only DeclValue gives an entry; each binding's refs are deduplicated with nub and lose the unqualified self-reference
TIO.readFile inside a SomeException catch; a read failure is a ParseFailure starting 'read failed: '
PSParser.parseModule on PSLexer.lexModule, then resFull on the partial result; an error from either stage is a ParseFailure from renderParserErrors
a partial parse is discarded when either stage fails

renderParserErrors: CSTErr.prettyPrintError on each error, joined with a newline and two spaces
extractStructure: computes declRanges once and runs each extractor over the ranges
chaseSignatures is extractSignature's results followed by extractClassMethods'; chaseForeignImports, chaseDataDecls and chaseFixities come from extractForeignImport, extractDataDecl and extractFixity
annotation fields stay empty and chaseTestCoverage stays Nothing, as in Chase.Parse.Haskell
valueBindingRefs: DeclValue only; the name and line come from CST.valName's token
refs come from collectValueBindingRefs, deduplicated with nub, without Ref Nothing of the binding's own name

notes: impQualifiedOnly is true exactly when the import has 'as', because in PureScript 'import M as X' brings names in only as X.name
impAlias is the 'as' name; no import list is ImportAll, a 'hiding' list is ImportHiding, any other list is ImportOnly
only ImportValue and ImportOp entries are listed; imported types, classes and kinds are not, since a Ref is always a value

extractImport: the module name via N.runModuleName, plus ' as Alias' when CST.impQual is set; an import list is never included
extractSignature: DeclSignature only; sigVerbatim is sliceLines over the declaration's whole range
extractClassMethods: the methods of a DeclClass with a 'where' block, through toMethodSig; a class without one gives []
toMethodSig: name and line from the method's Labeled (Name Ident) wrapper; sigVerbatim is that line with T.stripStart
extractForeignImport: DeclForeign only; ForeignValue is named by identText, ForeignData and ForeignKind by N.runProperName
sigVerbatim is the declaration's whole range
extractDataDecl: DeclData, DeclType and DeclNewtype render their whole range, named by dataHdName
DeclClass, DeclInstanceChain and DeclDerive render their first line; an instance or derive is named by its class's N.runProperName, so several instances of one class share a name
extractFixity: DeclFixity only; the first line, and one operator name from N.runOpName for FixityValue or FixityType
collectValueBindingRefs: an Unconditional binding walks its Where; a Guarded one walks each GuardedExpr
collectFromWhere: refs from the expression and from every binding in its where-clause via collectFromLetBinding, in one list
collectFromGuardedExpr: refs from each PatternGuard's expression via collectFromPatternGuard and from the guard's Where; binders on the left of '<-' are not refs
collectFromPatternGuard: refs from the PatternGuard's expression only
collectFromLetBinding: LetBindingSignature gives []; LetBindingName goes through collectValueBindingRefs; LetBindingPattern walks its Where and ignores the pattern
collectFromExpr: ExprIdent gives Ref with the qualifier from CST.qualModule, if any, and the name from identText; this is the reference that coverage counts
ExprConstructor, ExprOpName, ExprSection, ExprHole and literals give []
ExprInfix walks both operands and the backticked operator expression; ExprOp walks only the operands
ExprLambda, ExprCase and DoBind walk bodies and scrutinees but not binders
ExprRecordAccessor walks the record expression; the field label is not a ref
collectFromRecordLabeled: RecordPun gives Ref Nothing of the punned name, since '{ foo }' means '{ foo: foo }'
RecordField walks the field's expression; the label is not a ref
collectFromRecordUpdate: RecordUpdateLeaf walks the new value; RecordUpdateBranch recurses through delimitedNonEmptyToList
collectFromGuarded: the same Unconditional and Guarded cases as collectValueBindingRefs, for case branches
collectFromDoStatement: DoLet walks its bindings; DoDiscard and DoBind walk the expression; DoBind's pattern is ignored
delimitedToList: CST.Wrapped with Nothing inside, such as '[]' or '{}', gives []; otherwise sepToList
delimitedNonEmptyToList: sepToList of the CST.Wrapped contents; never []
sepToList: the head followed by map snd of the tail, which drops each separator SourceToken
declRanges: (declaration, start, end) with end = max start (next start - 1), and totalLines for the last
the max keeps the range from running backwards when two declarations start on the same line
declStartLine: the line of each declaration's first token via tokenLine: the keyword for most forms, the name token for DeclValue and DeclSignature
covers every CST.Declaration constructor, including DeclKindSignature and DeclRole
sliceLines: 1-indexed and inclusive; the start is clamped with max 0, and trailing lines for which T.strip gives '' are dropped before T.intercalate joins the rest
blank lines inside the range are kept
sliceFirstLine: drop (max 0 (startL - 1)) and take the head, so the 1-indexed line; '' past the end of the file
identText: CST.getIdent, used everywhere an Ident becomes Text
tokenLine: srcLine of srcStart of tokRange of tokAnn: the 1-indexed line a SourceToken starts on

decisions.name: StaticReferenceScanNotHPC
decisions.what: Coverage is found by walking each test file's AST for references, not by running the tests under HPC
why: HPC needs the test suite built and run with coverage and its .tix files read, which ties chase to the build system and test runner.
A static scan only parses the test sources: no build, no execution.
A reference is not proof of a behavioural test. A test may mention foo without checking it. 'no test references' is the useful signal: it almost always means untested.

decisions.name: ReferencesResolvedThroughImports
decisions.what: Each reference is resolved to the module that defines it through the imports of the file it appears in, and the index is keyed by (module, name)
why: Until 2026-10-24 the index was keyed by bare name, so two modules that both defined parse were each shown as tested by every test that called either (probe U5).
A qualified reference Q.f resolves to every module imported as Q, or imported under its own name Q with no alias, whose import list lets f through.
An unqualified reference f resolves to the referring module and to every module imported unqualified whose import list lets f through.

No module's export list is read, so an unqualified name in a file with several open imports is credited to each of them. That over-counts only among modules the file imports, which is where the name has to come from.

decisions.name: TopLevelFunBindOnly
decisions.what: In Haskell only top-level FunBinds become test bindings
why: A test is nearly always 'testFooHandlesX = ...', which is a FunBind. A pattern binding such as '(a, b) = setup' produces values, not a test.
References inside nested let and where bindings are still collected, because collectVarsIn walks the whole enclosing FunBind; they are credited to the enclosing binding.

decisions.name: SelfReferencesAreDropped
decisions.what: buildTestIndex drops a reference that resolves to the referring binding itself
why: A recursive helper would otherwise be listed as tested by itself.
The comparison is on the resolved module and name, so a qualified self-reference is dropped too, and a function in another module with the same name is still credited.

decisions.name: SYBTraversalForRobustness
decisions.what: collectVarsIn uses SYB's everything over the Data instance instead of a hand-written HsExpr traversal
why: HsExpr has dozens of constructors and ghc-lib-parser adds more between versions; a hand-written traversal misses a new constructor without a warning.
SYB.everything visits every subterm and applies the HsVar query wherever it matches, so new constructors are covered with no change here.
The cost is the syb dependency and generic dispatch, which is invisible at chase's scale.

decisions.name: TestFileDispatchByExtension
decisions.what: parseTestFile sends .purs files to parsePureScriptTestFile and every other file to parseHaskellTestFile
why: The two parsers share nothing: the Haskell one walks ghc-lib-parser's AST with SYB, the PureScript one uses Chase.Parse.PureScript.scanTestBindings, which walks the CST itself.
The callers pass only .hs and .purs files, so the Haskell branch acting as the default never sees anything else in practice.

openIssues.name: HigherOrderReferencesMissed
openIssues.what: Some ways a test can reach a function leave no reference for the walk to see
why: Missed: names produced by Template Haskell splices (ghc-lib-parser does not run them), calls made through instance dispatch or Generic deriving, and functions reached only through a record field or class method whose own name never appears in the test.
A reference through a re-exporting module resolves to the re-exporting module, not the defining one, because export lists are not read.
These are limits of a static scan without name resolution.

notes: takeExtension '.purs' goes to parsePureScriptTestFile; anything else goes to parseHaskellTestFile
a file that fails to parse is Left ParseFailure; the callers print a warning and skip it
Chase.Parse.Haskell.parseHsModule, then scanTestFile with moduleNameOf; a file without a module header has module ''
Chase.Parse.PureScript.scanTestBindings, repackaged as one TestBinding per value binding, each carrying the file's imports

scanTestFile: one TestBinding per top-level FunBind, each with HSP.importInfosOf of the module, computed once
pattern bindings, instances and type, class and data declarations give none
fromDecl: ValD FunBind gives a singleton with the name from fun_id, the line from startLine and refs from collectVarsIn of fun_matches, deduplicated with nub

notes: Ref (Just q): impModule of each import whose impAlias, or impModule when there is no alias, equals q, and whose impNames lets the name through
Ref Nothing: the referring module itself, plus impModule of each import that is not impQualifiedOnly and lets the name through
ImportAll lets every name through, ImportOnly only the listed ones, ImportHiding all but the listed ones
the result is deduplicated with nub; an unqualified name always resolves at least to the referring module
one index entry per (resolved module, refName) for every Ref of every TestBinding
a Ref that resolves to the binding's own module and name is dropped
within an entry, TestRefs are deduplicated by trModule and trFunction and sorted by trSrcLine
consumes: Chase.Callers.buildCallerIndex, which builds the same index from source directories as a call graph

notes: looks up (chaseModuleName, name) for every signature, foreign import and pattern, in that order
a name with no refs gets [], not a missing key, so Chase.Render prints 'no test references'
always sets chaseTestCoverage to Just
consumes: Chase.Pipeline.applyPasses, after attachAnnotations, only when cfgTestRoots is non-empty

collectVarsIn: SYB.everything with an HsVar query over any Data value reachable from a FunBind's MatchGroup
only HsVar in expression position: constructors, patterns, types and record field labels give nothing
returns refOf of each name, repeats included; fromDecl deduplicates
refOf: isQual_maybe: a qualified RdrName gives Ref (Just qualifier) name, any other gives Ref Nothing name
rdrNameToText: occNameString of rdrNameOcc; a copy of the helper in Chase.Parse.Haskell, which does not export it
startLine: srcSpanStartLine of a RealSrcSpan, 0 for an UnhelpfulSpan; a copy of the helper in Chase.Parse.Haskell

decisions.name: CallGraphIsTheCoverageIndex
decisions.what: The call graph is Chase.Coverage's reference index built from source directories instead of test directories
why: Coverage parses every binding, collects the references in its body and inverts them. Over source files, that inversion is who calls what, which is what an invariant's consumes records.
chase-annotate fills consumes from this index, so the model is never asked for callers. Asked for them, a local 7B returned module names from the %uses lines.

decisions.name: ScanTheCabalSourceDirs
decisions.what: The scan reads the hs-source-dirs of the nearest .cabal file's library, executable and common stanzas instead of walking the project tree
why: Walking pelotero-engine's tree reached script/concat_archive/, which holds concatenated dumps that are not valid Haskell, and .direnv/flake-inputs/, which holds the source of every flake input. Each file failed to parse and the warnings buried the result.
hs-source-dirs is the build's own definition of the source tree.
Test suites and benchmarks are left out: a test calling a function is coverage, and it would bury the real consumers.

notes: walks up from the source's directory, at most 40 levels, to the first directory with a .cabal file; with several, the first in listDirectory's order is used
spRoots are the hs-source-dirs that exist, joined to the .cabal file's directory
with no .cabal file, or none of its directories existing, spRoots is the source's own directory and spSource says why
consumes: app-annotate/Main.hs main, when no --roots are given

sourceDirsFromCabal: tracks the stanza by lines starting in column zero; only library, executable and common stanzas are read
reads hs-source-dirs and indented continuation lines without ':'; commas and spaces both separate entries; the result is deduplicated with nub
for chase.cabal it returns vendor/purescript-cst, src/annotations, src/core, src/codebase, src/bridge, app, app-annotate and app-unison

notes: Chase.Sources.findSourceFiles over each of spRoots, Chase.Coverage.parseTestFile on each file, then Chase.Coverage.buildTestIndex
prints two 'callers:' lines: spSource, and how many files parsed and how many names are referenced
files that fail to parse are listed only when verbose; they contribute nothing

callersOf: Map.findWithDefault [] for (modName, name); same-module callers are kept

notes: callersOf rendered as 'Module.function', deduplicated with nub, without the name's own definition
consumes: Chase.GraceBridge.toModuleAnnotations, which uses it as each generated invariant's consumes

renderCallers: a '%callers MODULE' line, then one line per name; a name with no callers says 'no callers found in the scanned source dirs'

decisions.name: OneLineFactsForLLMScannability
decisions.what: Every annotation renders as one line per fact, indented two spaces under the signature it describes
why: The reader is a model with a context budget, and wrapped paragraphs cost tokens and hide structure.
The sigils (! fact, > consumed by, ? coverage) let the reader pick out facts by kind.
The indentation ties each fact to its function when many functions share a module.

decisions.name: ImportsCollapseAndDropNames
decisions.what: Each import becomes one %uses line without its name list
why: Knowing that a module uses Data.List matters more to the reader than knowing it imported sort and nub.
Long multi-line import lists are a large share of the tokens in raw Haskell source.

decisions.name: CoverageIsSuppressedWhenNotAnalyzed
decisions.what: With chaseTestCoverage Nothing no ? lines are printed; with Just, every signature, foreign import and pattern gets one
why: Nothing keeps structure-only output clean.
With Just, 'no test references' is printed for untested names, because the gaps are what the user is looking for.
The Maybe lives on ChaseFile, so the renderer is driven by the data alone.

renderChaseFile: fixed order: %file and %mod, %ext, %fixity, %uses, %const, %machine and %topology, data declarations, %foreign, patterns, signatures, %decision, %open_issue, %parse_error
the order is part of the format: a reader prompted with the format expects it
each section helper returns [] for empty input, so an empty section leaves no header
renderExtensions: one '%ext' line with the names joined by T.intercalate ', ', followed by a blank line
renderFixities: a '%fixity' line, then each fixVerbatim indented two spaces
renderImports: one '%uses' line per import from collapseImport; an import that collapses to '' is dropped
collapseImport: T.unwords of T.words joins the lines, T.takeWhile (/= '(') drops the name list, and the 'import ' prefix is stripped
'qualified', 'as X' and 'hiding' survive because they come before the '('
renderConstants: '%const NAME = VALUE', and when there are notes '  -- ' and the notes joined with '; '
a BugNote is printed with the 'BUG: ' prefix
renderTopologies: a '%machine NAME vertices=A,B' line, then one '%topology FROM -> {TO, ...}' line per transition
renderDataDecls: each cddVerbatim followed by a blank line; cddName is not printed
renderForeignImports: a '%foreign' header and then renderSig for each foreign import, so invariants and ? lines attach to them as to signatures
renderPatternsWithInvariants: the same block as renderSig for each Pattern, keyed by patName, with no header line
renderSignaturesWithInvariants: renderSig for each Signature, with the invariants as an association list keyed by invFunction
lookup returns the first invariant with a name, so a second invariant for the same name in chaseInvariants is never printed
renderSig: the verbatim text, then '  ! ' lines from invLines, '  > consumed by: ' lines from invConsumes, the body hint indented two spaces, the ? line from renderCoverage, and a blank line
renderCoverage: Nothing gives []; Just without an entry for the name gives []; an empty entry gives '  ? no test references'
otherwise one '  ? tested by: ' line with renderTestRef of each ref joined by ', '
renderTestRef: trModule and trFunction joined by '.'; trSrcLine is kept in TestRef but not printed
renderDecisions: '%decision NAME' and the lines 'what:', 'why:' and 'affects:', then a blank line; affects is joined with ', ' and printed even when empty
renderOpenIssues: '%open_issue NAME', 'what:' and 'why:', then 'blocking:' and 'affects:' only when non-empty, then a blank line
renderParseErrors: a blank line and one '%parse_error' line per entry of chaseParseErrors
no parser fills chaseParseErrors, so this prints nothing in practice; Chase.Pipeline.runBundled writes its own %parse_error block for a file that fails

decisions.name: AttachReplacesNotMerges
decisions.what: attachAnnotations replaces chaseConstants, chaseInvariants, chaseDecisions, chaseOpenIssues and chaseTopologies with the module's annotations
why: No parser fills those fields, so replacing and merging give the same result today.
If a parser ever extracts annotations from comments, merging becomes a real choice; replace keeps the JSON file the single source, and a merge has to be added on purpose.

decisions.name: DriftCheckerScopeIsLocal
decisions.what: checkAnnotationDrift checks names against the same file's signatures, foreign imports and patterns only
why: Checking across modules would mean collecting every file's names before checking any, a two-pass pipeline.

consumes entries are not checked. chase-annotate now generates them from the call graph in Chase.Callers, so generated ones are correct when written; hand-written ones and ones that go stale after a rename are not caught.
Open-issue blocking entries are not checked, since they usually name features or other systems rather than functions.

decisions.name: CoverageIndexIsBuiltOnce
decisions.what: buildTestIndexOrEmpty parses every test file once, before the source pass, and every source file shares the index
why: Parsing the tests once per source file would cost sources times tests; once costs sources plus tests.
With no test roots the index is Map.empty and no test file is read.
A test file that fails to parse is reported and contributes nothing; the rest of the index is unaffected.

decisions.name: BundleBytesDependOnlyOnInputs
decisions.what: The bundle's preamble carries the roots and file counts and nothing that depends on when chase ran
why: A %generated timestamp stood second in the preamble until 2026-10-24. open-slop's ingest skips a file whose content hash it already has, and the timestamp made every bundle new, so every bundle was re-embedded on every ingest (probe U3).
Files are found in sorted order by Chase.Sources.findSourceFiles, so the order of the blocks depends only on the tree.

decisions.name: ChecksForEmptyAndFabricatedAnnotations
decisions.what: Besides name checks, checkAnnotationDrift flags invariants that restate the type and open issues that claim something absent that the file defines
why: Measured on 2026-09-26 with a local 7B annotating Pelotero.DB.Pool: eight of its ten invariants restated the type in English, and every name check passed.
Told that, its next attempt replaced the invariants with open issues saying functions in the file were 'not implemented'.
Both failures are mechanical, so they are checked mechanically: saysSomethingNew for the first, claimsAbsence for the second.

openIssues.name: ExecutablesShareTheModuleNameMain
openIssues.what: Annotations are keyed by module name, and chase's three executables (app/Main.hs, app-annotate/Main.hs, app-unison/ChaseUnison.hs) are all module Main
why: attachAnnotations looks a file up by chaseModuleName alone, so a 'Main' entry would attach to every executable in a run that includes them, and its names would be reported as drift in the other two.
This file therefore has no entry for Main, and the reference bundle in .inference covers src only.
A fix needs a key that tells executables apart, such as the source path relative to the project root for modules named Main.
blocking: annotating executables in a project with more than one

openIssues.name: PartialRunsReportOtherModules
openIssues.what: A run over some of a project's source directories reports the annotated modules in the other directories as matching no source file
why: unmatchedAnnotations compares the annotation keys with the modules parsed in this run, and a run over src/core does not parse Chase.Types in src/annotations.
Limiting the report to modules whose files would fall under the run's roots needs a guess from module name to path.

defaultConfig: no source or test roots, cfgOutputDir 'chase', no bundle file, no annotations, cfgVerbose False
callers override fields with record update; nothing is read from the environment
runChase: builds the test index first, then runs runPerFile or runBundled by cfgBundleFile
after the source pass, prints one 'drift:' line per entry of unmatchedAnnotations
unmatchedAnnotations: one 'annotations for module M match no source file' for each of Map.keys of the annotations for which Set.member in the parsed set is false
a module whose file failed to parse is not in the parsed set, so it is reported here as well as by the parse warning

notes: Map.empty without touching the filesystem when cfgTestRoots is empty
Chase.Sources.findSourceFiles over each test root, then Chase.Coverage.parseTestFile on each .hs and .purs file
a test file that fails to parse prints 'WARN: test parse failed' and contributes nothing
with cfgVerbose prints 'test roots:', 'scan PATH' per file and 'index N distinct names referenced by tests'
one .chase file per source file under cfgOutputDir, at mkOutputPath
a parse failure prints a warning and writes nothing for that file
drift warnings for each file are printed as it is processed
returns the Set of module names parsed, for unmatchedAnnotations
every file is parsed and rendered first, counting successes and failures in IORefs, then the preamble is rendered with the counts and the whole bundle written with one TIO.writeFile
a file that fails to parse gets a block from renderFailureBlock with its %parse_error, so the bundle shows every file
returns the Set of module names parsed, for unmatchedAnnotations

applyPasses: attachAnnotations, then Chase.Coverage.attachCoverage only when the test roots are non-empty
with no test roots chaseTestCoverage stays Nothing and no ? lines are printed
renderPreamble: '%bundle chase v1', '%roots' with the roots joined by ', ', '%files N ok, M failed', then a comment block explaining the format to the reader
renderBundleBlock: a blank line, '=== BEGIN PATH ===' with relativeToRoots of the file, a blank line, then the rendered ChaseFile
renderFailureBlock: the same BEGIN line as renderBundleBlock followed by '%parse_error' and the parser's message

notes: Map.lookup by chaseModuleName; no entry leaves the file unchanged
replaces the five annotation fields; see decision AttachReplacesNotMerges
the valid names are chaseSignatures, chaseForeignImports and chasePatterns; data types, constructors and class names are not valid names
reports invariants, decision affects and open-issue affects naming something outside that set
reports an invariant with lines whose identifiers, by saysSomethingNew, add nothing to its signature
reports an open issue whose what or why trips claimsAbsence while its affects names functions the file defines
consumes, blocking and constants are not checked
consumes: Chase.Pipeline.runPerFile and Chase.Pipeline.runBundled, which print each warning
Chase.GraceBridge.generateWithDriftFeedback, which feeds the warnings into the next prompt

notes: (invariants that have a signature, have lines and pass saysSomethingNew, length of checkAnnotationDrift)
more good invariants is better; on a tie, fewer warnings
consumes: Chase.GraceBridge.generateWithDriftFeedback, to keep the best attempt instead of the last

saysSomethingNew: true when identifiersIn of the lines, lower-cased, has a token that is neither in identifiersIn of the signature nor the function's own name
an invariant whose new fact is plain English, such as 'reads the settings from environment variables', is flagged although it is informative; that is why the result is a warning and not a rejection
claimsAbsence: case-insensitive substring match against a fixed list such as 'not implemented', 'is missing', 'does not exist' and 'should read'
the list was matched against chase's own open issues, which do not trip it, and against the fabricated ones a 7B produced, which all did
identifiersIn: tokens split on anything but letters, digits, '.', '_' and quote marks, with edge punctuation dropped
a token counts when it has an inner dot, an inner or leading capital, a digit or an underscore; a two-character token counts only with both a digit and a letter, so 'v2' counts and 'is' does not
mkOutputPath: cfgOutputDir </> relativeToRoots of the file with its extension replaced by .chase
relativeToRoots: the path relative to the first root that makeRelative actually shortens it against
a file under no root gives takeFileName of the path, so two such files with the same name collide

decisions.name: BridgeIsASeparateSublibrary
decisions.what: chase-grace-bridge is a public sublibrary under src/bridge, outside the main chase library
why: grace brings megaparsec, an HTTP client and its own closure. chase's deterministic pipeline (parse, render, drift-check) needs none of it.
With the split, the chase library and executable build without network or model code.
Replacing grace, or adding another backend, is confined to src/bridge and app-annotate.

decisions.name: GraceTemplateIsExternalized
decisions.what: The prompt is grace/genAnnotations.ffg, a typed Grace function, not a string in this module
why: Grace turns the function's return type into a JSON Schema for the model's structured output, and the result is decoded into GenAnnotations.
The prompt can be changed without rebuilding chase. It is installed as a cabal data file, so chase-annotate finds it wherever it runs.
The records GenArgs, GenAnnotations, GenInvariant, GenDecision and GenOpenIssue mirror the schema; their field names are the schema's field names through Generic.

decisions.name: BestAttemptWithBoundedRetries
decisions.what: generateWithDriftFeedback retries with the previous attempt's warnings up to maxRetries times and returns the best attempt, not the last
why: chase cannot check what a note says, but it can check which names it uses, whether it restates the type, and whether an open issue denies code that exists.

Measured 2026-09-26: the first attempt had ten invariants, eight of them restatements; the second, given those warnings, deleted the invariants and returned eight fabricated open issues. Keeping the last attempt threw away the better one.
maxRetries bounds the loop, so a model that never produces a clean result still stops.

decisions.name: NotesCheckedAgainstTheirOwnFunction
decisions.what: Each generated note's identifiers must appear in its own function's signature or definition, or the note is removed and reported
why: With the source in the prompt, the model began naming things from the right file but the wrong function: for 'release = Pool.release' it wrote that release uses dbPoolSize from DBConfig. dbPoolSize is in the module, so a module-wide check passed it.
A note with no identifier is kept, because it cannot be checked this way; saysSomethingNew in Chase.Pipeline judges those.

decisions.name: InvariantFieldNamedBody
decisions.what: GenInvariant's list of facts is called body, not lines
why: Under RecordWildCards a field named lines would shadow Prelude.lines in every function that unpacks a GenInvariant.

The template's schema uses the same name, because the schema's field names come from the record. The annotations file still calls the field notes: app-annotate's invariantsToJSON writes it under that key.

decisions.name: DuplicateRecordFieldsForJsonShape
decisions.what: DuplicateRecordFields is on because GenDecision and GenOpenIssue both have name, what, why and affects
why: The schema mirrors the annotations format, where decisions and open issues share those field names.
Prefixed Haskell names would put the prefixes into the schema the model sees, or need a translation step on output.

notes: Grace.Interpret.load on Path graceTemplate AsCode, decoded as GenArgs -> IO GenAnnotations
the template is read once; each call of the returned function makes one model request
the first call has driftWarnings []; each later call gets the previous attempt's warnings
each attempt goes through dropUnsupportedNotes, toModuleAnnotations and mergeForCheck, then Pipeline.checkAnnotationDrift and Pipeline.annotationScore
an attempt with no warnings is returned at once; otherwise, after maxRetries retries, the best attempt by (good invariants, warnings) is returned with its warnings
the model and endpoint are not known here; grace reads OPENAI_BASE_URL

dropUnsupportedNotes: for each invariant, a line is kept unless noteIdentifiers finds a word that is not a case-insensitive substring of the signature plus definitionOf the function
an invariant left with no lines is dropped, and each removed line produces a warning naming up to three of the missing words
definitionOf: from the first line starting with the name and a space or tab, through each following line that is indented or starts with the name again
a text scan, not a parser; it errs towards taking too much, which makes dropUnsupportedNotes lenient
noteIdentifiers: code-shaped tokens by the same test as Chase.Pipeline's identifiersIn, plus words the model wrote in single quotes

notes: annConstants and annTopologies are always [], since the template does not produce them
each invariant's invConsumes is Callers.callerNames of the module and function; the model is not asked for callers
decisions and open issues are copied field for field

mergeForCheck: copies the five annotation fields onto the parsed ChaseFile so checkAnnotationDrift sees the real signatures
the result is never written or rendered

decisions.name: PathSegmentsAreEncoded
decisions.what: The project and branch names are percent-encoded before they go into the URL path
why: A contributor branch such as @harry/feature has a '/' that would otherwise split the path, and the request would go to a route that does not exist.

openIssues.name: UnusedEndpoints
openIssues.what: getDefinitions, getDependents and segmentRefs are exported but nothing in chase calls them
why: collectSkeleton resolves each definition with getDefinition one at a time, and invariants' consumes are written by hand, so the batch endpoint, the dependents endpoint and segment references are dead code today.

newCodebase: one http-client Manager from defaultManagerSettings, which has no TLS, so the base URL must be http
a trailing '/' on the base URL is dropped
segment: T.unpack of TE.decodeUtf8 of urlEncode False of the UTF-8 bytes
apiGet: GET BASE/api/projects/PROJECT/branches/BRANCH/ENDPOINT with mkParams as the query string
a bad URL, an HTTP exception, a status outside 200 to 299, and a JSON decode failure each come back as Left with a prefix: 'bad request url', 'http error', 'http CODE', 'decode error'
mkParams: drops parameters whose value is Nothing and UTF-8 encodes the rest
showBody: the response body decoded with TEE.lenientDecode, for error messages
listNamespace: the 'list' endpoint with namespace and relativeTo; Nothing for the namespace lists the branch root
getDefinition: apiGet on the 'getDefinition' endpoint with one 'names' parameter; relativeTo is sent only when it is Just
getDefinitions: the 'getDefinition' endpoint with the names parameter repeated, so the server renders all of them against one pretty-print environment
valueToText: Just for a JSON String, Nothing for anything else; an Annotation's contents is a hash only when it is a string
renderSegments: T.concat of segText; annotations are dropped
segmentRefs: (fqn, hash) for each segment whose annTag ends in 'Reference' and has both fields
displayObjectSegments: the segments of a UserObject or BuiltinObject; [] for a MissingObject

decisions.name: WalkFirstFetchAfter
decisions.what: The namespace walk only lists namespaces; every definition is fetched afterwards, in a bounded pool
why: Listing first shows every name a hash has before anything is fetched, so each definition is fetched once and its aliases are known.
planResolution can then drop constructors, accessor satellites and folded getters without fetching them.
Each in-flight fetch holds a full pretty-print environment in UCM. 16 at once made the kernel kill UCM; resolveConcurrency is 4.

decisions.name: DependenciesSkippedAtTheRootOnly
decisions.what: lib and namespaces named like versioned dependencies are skipped only at the branch root
why: A Unison project keeps its dependencies under lib at the branch root. Deeper down, a namespace called lib, or one ending in three numeric parts such as v_1_2_3, is the project's own code.
Until 2026-10-24 both were skipped at any depth, so such user code was left out of the bundle.

decisions.name: FailuresDegradeVisibly
decisions.what: A definition that still fails after retries is rendered from the listing and reported, never passed off as resolved
why: A term falls back to its listing signature and a type to an empty declaration, so the bundle is complete in names.
reportFailures prints the count and up to ten names to stderr, so a degraded bundle is never mistaken for a clean one.

openIssues.name: RenderSkeletonDuplicatesRenderAnnotated
openIssues.what: renderSkeleton and renderEntry repeat what Chase.Unison.Annotate.renderAnnotated renders, and nothing calls them
why: chase-unison renders through renderAnnotated, with empty annotations when there are none, so the two renderers can drift apart unseen.

resolveConcurrency: 4: the number of getDefinition requests in flight at once; bounded by UCM's memory, not CPU
resolveRetries: 3 attempts per definition before it is degraded; see fetchWithRetry
defaultSkip: ["lib"]: names skipped at the branch root by shouldSkipNamespace
isDependencyNamespace: true when the last three '_'-separated parts of the name are all digits, as in runarorama_postgres_2_5_1
shouldSkipNamespace: true when the name is in the skip list or isDependencyNamespace holds; handleChild consults it only when the parent namespace is the root

notes: walkNs from the given root with defaultSkip, then planResolution, then resolveEntry for each entry through mapPool resolveConcurrency
prints the definition count, the number to resolve and the concurrency to stderr before fetching
Left only when a namespace listing fails; a failed definition fetch degrades that entry instead

reportFailures: nothing for no failures; otherwise a WARNING with the count, a hint to set resolveConcurrency = 1, and the first ten failures
walkNs: one listNamespace call per namespace; the root is listed with Nothing
a failed listing stops the whole walk with Left 'list NAMESPACE: ...'
foldChildren: handleChild over the children in listing order, stopping at the first Left
handleChild: a term or type is added to the accumulator under its hash with its full name from joinNs
a namespace is walked unless the parent is the root and shouldSkipNamespace holds
addReq: Map.insertWith on the hash: the first kind seen for a hash wins, and later sightings only add names
planResolution: types are always fetched; terms whose listing tag contains 'constructor' are dropped
a getter is a dotted name that has both NAME.set and NAME.modify among the terms; its .set and .modify satellites are dropped
a getter whose owning type, the name without its last segment, is in the walk is folded onto that type as a field name instead of being fetched
isConstructorReq: True for a ReqTerm whose tag, lower-cased with T.toLower, contains 'constructor'
resolveEntry: fetches by mostQualified of the sorted names, the name with the most segments, which is the least likely to be ambiguous
a term without a fetched signature falls back to its listing signature; a type without a fetched declaration gets an empty one; either way the second element names the failure
fetchWithRetry: retries getDefinition with a delay that starts at 250000 microseconds and doubles after each failure
firstValue: the first element of Map.elems, so a single-name response is read without matching its hash key
mostQualified: the last of the names as sortNames orders them; '' for none
mapPool: mapConcurrently with a QSem of n around each call, so at most n run at once; results keep the input order
oneLineSig: T.unwords of T.words, so a multi-line signature becomes one line
buildSkeleton: entries with attachFields applied, sorted by their bestName
attachFields: adds the folded field names to a type entry's field list, deduplicated and sorted with dedupSort
stripAccessorSuffix: T.stripSuffix '.set', and failing that T.stripSuffix '.modify'; Nothing for any other name
lastSeg: last of T.splitOn on '.', which never fails because T.splitOn always returns at least one part
dropLastSeg: T.splitOn on '.', all but the last part via safeInit, rejoined with T.intercalate; '' for a name with one segment
sortNames: sortOn the key (T.count of '.', T.length, the name), so the least qualified name comes first and ties break alphabetically
bestName: the head of the list, which after sortNames is the least qualified name; '(anonymous)' for an empty list
used by planResolution, buildSkeleton and renderEntry
renderSkeleton: %codebase, %root and %defs lines, then renderEntry for each entry; see open issue RenderSkeletonDuplicatesRenderAnnotated
renderEntry: a term as 'NAME : SIG   ~HASH' or a type as 'type[TAG] NAME   ~HASH' with its declaration and fields, then an '> aka:' line for the other names
joinNs: PARENT.SEGMENT, or SEGMENT when the parent is the root
nsLabel: '(root)' when T.null holds for the namespace, else the namespace; used in walkNs error messages

decisions.name: OneModuleForTheWholeCodebase
decisions.what: A Unison codebase's annotations are one ModuleAnnotations entry, named after the project
why: A codebase has namespaces, not modules, and definitions are named by their full names.
chase-unison looks the project name up in the annotations file and uses emptyAnnotations when it is absent.

decisions.name: InvariantsAttachByAnyName
decisions.what: An invariant attaches to a definition by any of its names, not only its best name
why: The drift check accepted an invariant written against an alias, because every name is valid, but only the best name's invariant was rendered, so the invariant vanished without a warning (probe U1).
A definition with invariants under two of its names shows both.

decisions.name: UnrenderedAnnotationsAreReported
decisions.what: Constants and topologies, which a Unison bundle does not render, are each reported in the drift warnings
why: They used to be ignored without a word, so an annotator could not tell they were not shown.

notes: a header with %codebase, %root and %defs and a comment block explaining the format, then each entry, then %decision and %open_issue blocks
each entry is followed by the '  ! ' and '  > consumed by: ' lines of every invariant keyed by one of its names, then its '> aka:' line
arDriftWarnings lists each constant and topology as not shown, each invariant name no definition has, and each decision or open-issue affects name no definition has
with emptyAnnotations the output is structure only

bestName: the first name, or '(anonymous)'; a copy of Chase.Unison.Extract.bestName
renderDecision: '%decision NAME', 'what:' and 'why:', and 'affects:' only when non-empty, then a blank line
renderOpenIssue: '%open_issue NAME', 'what:' and 'why:', then 'blocking:' and 'affects:' only when non-empty, then a blank line
